If the discriminant is positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex ones.

Take the derivative of f(x), which gives you dy/dx. Set that equal to zero and solve for x. These are your critical points. Then plug each x value back into the original function to get the corresponding y values. Those (x,y) pairs are your stationary points.
